clue.text: American lawyer in dash reaches Dutch town

indicators.note: in tells us the lawyer sits inside the dash

parts.note: an em is a printer's dash
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A US attorney sprints off to a town in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' here is not a sprint but the em, a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a cheese-making town in North Holland.

clue.text: Asian joint said to be very small

indicators.note: said means the phrase is spoken and we enter what it sounds like

parts.note: a Thai is an Asian person and a knee is a joint: Thai knee

explanation.surface: An Asian restaurant or bar is reputed to be cramped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a bar or eatery; it is the knee, attached to a Thai.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: minute, diminutive.

clue.text: Hero from Left supporting response in union ceremony

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting puts the L beneath the other piece

parts.note: I do is what each partner says at a wedding

explanation.surface: A champion is taken from the left-wing side to back a wedding vow.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a person admired as a hero.

clue.text: Pro runs in pack — flanker?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: in places the runs inside the pack

parts.note: a wad is a bundle or pack
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A professional rugby player charges with the pack: is he a flanker?
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union a flanker is one of the forwards, so the question mark marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A flanker is one type of rugby forward, defined by example.

clue.text: As calm and troubled time among faceless

indicators.note: among puts the time inside the other word

parts.note: faceless means without identity, nameless

explanation.surface: Seemingly a description of a state of mind both calm and troubled, amid faceless crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the pair itself: calm and troubled are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are opposite in meaning are described as opposites in this adjectival sense.

clue.text: Book opening put back with journalist taking hint

parts.note: ED is short for editor
to get wind of something is to have a hint of it

indicators.note: put back means the word for an opening is reversed

parts.note: a door is an opening

explanation.surface: A book's opening is restored after a journalist gets a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: DOOR reversed gives ROOD. The Mystery of Edwin Drood is Dickens's unfinished novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mystery of Edwin Drood is the final, unfinished Dickens novel.

clue.text: Was upset about an inflamed rash?

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other
upset in a down clue turns the word over, reading backwards

parts.note: was, in the sense of existed, means lived
inflamed skin is red

explanation.surface: Someone was distressed by an angry skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LIVED into DEVIL, which goes 'about' ARED. 'rash' is the adjective reckless, not a skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, rash person is a thrill-seeker; the question mark flags the adjective-to-noun stretch.

clue.text: Beer that's mine around noon

indicators.note: around tells us the mine goes round the noon letter

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A miner fancies a beer at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint is a standard measure of beer in a British pub.

clue.text: £25 envelope for rising subscription — thousand for Tees?

indicators.note: an envelope for something wraps around it

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: dues are a membership subscription
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A cash envelope for membership fees, and a thousand for the setter?
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is the name this setter signs under.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters publish under assumed names, so Tees is an example of a pen name.

clue.text: Tree bark used by settlers

definitions.meaning: the hawthorn, or May tree, is also known by this name
a bark or barque is a sailing ship; this one carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620

explanation.surface: Tree bark used by early settlers for building.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn bears the name, as did the Pilgrim Fathers' ship to New England.

clue.text: Idiosyncrasy regularly detected in frauds

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A quirk turns up at regular intervals in cases of fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing craze or personal whim; both senses are close to a quirk.

clue.text: Champion lacking height succeeded in love

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for height is dropped

parts.note: a champion is a hero
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A short champion found success in romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, and the word also names erotic desire.

clue.text: Bird Madagascan primate skinned

indicators.note: skinned means the outer letters are peeled away

parts.note: the lemur is the primate native to Madagascar

explanation.surface: A bird is something a Madagascan primate has skinned.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Plant in ancient river deity protects

indicators.note: protects means the deity surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a deity is a god
olden means of old, ancient

explanation.surface: A god of an ancient river guards a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldenrod is a yellow-flowered plant of the genus Solidago.

clue.text: Eating to excess: Lou's gut struggles to contain ton

indicators.note: to contain means the scrambled letters hold the other word
struggles suggests the letters wrestling into a new order

explanation.surface: Lou overeats, and his stomach strains to hold a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lou's gut' reads as a man's belly, but the apostrophe-s just supplies an S; 'struggles' makes GLUTOUS, and 'to contain' sets the weight in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greedy for food: overeating is the core of gluttony.

clue.text: Fabulous line, ready to broadcast, conveys 27

indicators.note: conveys means the scrambled word carries the other piece within
to broadcast means scatter, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: 27 down is INFO, and gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A fabulous line, ready to go on air, carries news.
explanation.walkthrough: '27' is a cross-reference to another answer, so a synonym of it is needed: British slang gen. 'to broadcast' makes EDARY, which 'conveys' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean famed as in a story, the stuff of myth.

clue.text: Eliot's village festival involves endless drink

indicators.note: involves means the festival wraps around the drink

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut

parts.note: Coke is a fizzy drink

explanation.surface: A poet's home village holds a festival with drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: East Coker is a Somerset village and one of T. S. Eliot's Four Quartets.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot's ashes lie in this Somerset village, which titles one of his Four Quartets.

clue.text: Times always collected by Detective Sergeant

indicators.note: collected by means taken inside the other piece

parts.note: ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A detective sergeant always picks up the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it means periods, as in olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural nouns for eras: in my day, in times past.

clue.text: Wants to be stopping nonsense writer

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap inside the other piece

parts.note: BS is slang shorthand for nonsense
urges are wants, desires

explanation.surface: Someone wants to stop a writer of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonsense writer' looks like Edward Lear; the writer is Anthony Burgess, author of A Clockwork Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Burgess wrote A Clockwork Orange, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: One with front garden in novel

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the van is the front, as in vanguard
to hoe is to work the garden

explanation.surface: Someone with a front garden appears in a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is Sir Walter Scott's novel of medieval England.

clue.text: United including only men in position to perform

indicators.note: including means the first word holds the second

parts.note: united means made one
a stag party or event is for men only

explanation.surface: A united team with a men-only line-up is ready to play.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor in front of the audience is ready to perform.

clue.text: Bowl over, taking time in fine weather

indicators.note: taking means the weather word takes in the other letter

parts.note: sun is fine weather

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowls an over, taking his time in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowl over' evokes cricket but means astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl over someone is to amaze or daze them.

clue.text: Cathedral's vergers recalled uniform for feast

parts.note: vergers read as verges, the edges: the edges of the word Cathedral are C and L, spelt out in full as C-AND-L

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: uniform means the same throughout

explanation.surface: Cathedral vergers called back to uniform for a religious feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vergers' are church officials in the surface; read as edges they are 'C and L', the AND included. 'recalled' reverses SAME to EMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlemas is the church festival on 2 February when candles are blessed.

clue.text: Lead-free transport gets attention

indicators.note: lead-free means the leading letter is removed

parts.note: to transport is to carry, bear

explanation.surface: Transport running on unleaded fuel gets noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone's ear is to have their attention.

clue.text: Party split by posh pairing

indicators.note: split by means the party is broken open by the next letter

parts.note: a do is a party
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A party divided by snobbery breaks up a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair, as of performers.

clue.text: Tongue almost swallowed by moggy?

parts.note: something swallowed by an animal is in it

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is lost

parts.note: moggy is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat almost gulps down someone's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' plays on the cat that got your tongue; it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of the Incas, also known as Quechua, is a tongue in the sense of a language.

clue.text: Citizen in film incarcerates the Rhode Island girl

indicators.note: incarcerates means locks up inside

parts.note: Citizen Kane is the Orson Welles film

explanation.surface: A citizen in a film imprisons a girl from Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Katherine is a female given name.

clue.text: Requiem mass inspires literary work

indicators.note: inspires means breathes in, so the words hold the answer inside

explanation.surface: A requiem mass prompts a writer's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is the Jane Austen novel.

clue.text: Data coming up concerning UK region

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue reads the pieces upwards

parts.note: of can mean concerning, as in tales of
NI is Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Data emerge about a region of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for information, a casual synonym for data.

clue.text: Odd characters leaving Georgian poet's country

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters go, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Eccentrics leave a Georgian poet's homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian poet' suggests a Georgian-era poet; Georgian only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is the poetic name for Ireland.

clue.text: Put down in Greater Manchester region

definitions.meaning: to put down a body is to inter it
a borough and town of Greater Manchester in north-west England

explanation.surface: A district of Greater Manchester is put down.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to lay in the ground; Bury is also a Greater Manchester town.

clue.text: Urchin for example reading again admits mistake

parts.note: R stands for reading, one of the three Rs

indicators.note: admits means lets the mistake in

parts.note: a muff is a fumble or mistake

explanation.surface: A street kid, reading over again, owns up to an error.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading, writing and arithmetic are the three Rs, so reading is R.
explanation.definitionFit: An urchin is one kind of scruffy, ragged child.
